result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give concrete, restrained plans that keep the screen still on open, use a single tinted status transition, and list clear leave-out decisions. B wins narrowly because its timing table gives an easing for every animated element and it covers more edge cases, such as a poll returning the same status and network failure. A gives easing for only some elements but handles live courier pin movement well. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give strong, concrete plans with plausible timings, no looping motion, explicit leave-out lists, and a one-time tint cue for status updates that arrive while someone is watching. B is slightly better: it explicitly lists what always stays still, handles an update landing mid-transition by retargeting, and treats the courier pin as a small, meaningful live indicator without inventing motion between server updates. A is equally disciplined, but its status-change sequence is longer, and it says less about the map and about overlapping updates.
